title: Recent vLLMs ask for too much memory: ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks
body: Since vLLM 0.2.5, I can no longer run a 4-bit AWQ Llama 2 70B model on four A10G GPUs, although older vLLM versions work. I also see problems when starting two 7B models on one A100 80GB GPU. For example, the second 7B model starts with gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 but fails at 0.4 with `ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks`, even though substantial GPU memory appears to remain. The two model configurations use maximum model lengths and maximum batched-token counts of 8192 and 4096.

symptoms_visible: Since vLLM 0.2.5, my Llama 2 70B 4-bit AWQ deployment no longer starts on four A10G GPUs, although it worked with older vLLM.
When I put two 7B models on one A100, the second model starts at gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 but reports no available memory for cache blocks at 0.4 even though more GPU memory appears to be free.
N0.label: N0 cache-block startup failures reported

symptoms_visible: The single 70B AWQ model still cannot start across four otherwise empty A10G GPUs on vLLM 0.2.5 or newer.
The same deployment starts on vLLM 0.2.4 and remains usable under long-running load.
N1.label: N1 clean multi-GPU regression established

symptoms_visible: On an affected large tensor-parallel deployment, I see about 22 GB free per GPU before the profiling forward pass and only about 0.26 GB free afterward.
The large-model startup still ends with very few or no GPU cache blocks.
N2.label: N2 profiling memory measurements collected

symptoms_visible: After I reverted the newer memory-profiling change, the cache-block startup message no longer appeared, but the same long-context query ran out of GPU memory.
N2_x.label: N2_x profiling revert aftermath

symptoms_visible: With eager execution enforced, my 70B AWQ model starts successfully across the four A10G GPUs without the no-cache-blocks error.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter-confirmed eager-mode workaround

question_patterns: For the four-A10G case, are those GPUs empty or shared with any other processes?
Is any other process consuming memory on the A10G GPUs when the 70B model starts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The four A10G GPUs are clean. Nothing else is running on them.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The GPUs are shared, and other processes already occupy most of their memory before vLLM starts.
Only a few megabytes are used by the driver; there are no other model-serving processes.

edges.comment: Reporter c4 answered the maintainer's question about whether the four-A10G setup was shared. Reporter c15 then emphasized that the primary chain is one 70B AWQ model sharded over clean GPUs, not the separate two-model case, and restated the vLLM 0.2.4 comparison.

question_patterns: Can you log the free GPU memory immediately before and after vLLM's profiling forward pass on an affected large tensor-parallel model?
What raw memory readings do you get around `profile_run()` during cache initialization?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my affected 70B deployment, I logged about 22 GB free on each 40 GB GPU before `profile_run()`. Immediately after it, only about 0.26 GB was free per GPU.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Free memory is essentially unchanged before and after the profiling pass, but vLLM still calculates zero cache blocks.
The exact readings vary slightly between GPUs, but each drops from roughly 22 GB free to less than 1 GB after the profiling pass.

edges.comment: Participant11 c16-c17 supplied raw instrumentation from another affected large tensor-parallel deployment: 70B BF16 on eight A100-40GB GPUs. This affected operator is explicitly folded into the simulated user side only for the shared profiling-memory diagnostic evidence; their hardware and model format are not attributed to the opening reporter.

solution.intent: Revert the newer GPU-memory profiling calculation so cache sizing again uses the older torch-allocation-based peak measurement.
solution.concrete_example: Locally revert the newer worker memory-profiling calculation and retry the same long-context workload.

edges.comment: Participant13 c22-c24 proposed reverting the profiling change, and the reporter tried it in c25-c27. It removed the title error but the same long-context query then hit GPU OOM, so reverting is not the accepted resolution. A later maintainer analysis in c29 also states that the newer accounting correctly includes non-torch allocations.

solution.intent: Keep the complete GPU-memory accounting rather than the unsafe local revert, and run the affected four-A10G 70B AWQ deployment with eager execution enforced to avoid the extra non-eager startup memory overhead.
solution.concrete_example: Restore the supported vLLM worker code and add `--enforce-eager` to the API server command, then start the same 70B AWQ deployment on the four clean A10G GPUs and verify the long-context workload before declaring it resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied the before/after free-memory readings and the final eager-mode outcome. Interpreting those readings as profiling-forward fragmentation or transient non-eager execution overhead, while retaining the accounting that includes NCCL, cuBLAS, and other non-torch allocations, is engineer-side synthesis from c17 and c29. The final accepted reporter result in c31 is specifically that eager execution makes the four-A10G 70B AWQ case work.

edges.comment: Participant1 first suggested eager execution in c0, but the reporter did not confirm it then and correctly noted that the regression began in vLLM 0.2.5. After the profiling-revert experiment failed under a long-context query and c29 clarified why the complete accounting should remain, the reporter confirmed in c31 that `--enforce_eager` solves the primary four-A10G 70B AWQ case.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted primary diagnosis at the level established by the thread: cache initialization measures a profiling/non-eager execution peak that leaves no safely calculated KV-cache blocks on the clean multi-GPU large-model setup; this is not evidence that the model weights themselves became larger.
Must recommend enforcing eager execution for the reporter's four-A10G 70B AWQ deployment, thereby avoiding the extra non-eager startup memory overhead.

Must ground the recommendation in the clean-GPU version regression and the measured drop in free memory across the profiling pass, rather than treating the visible cache-block error as proof that the GPUs are genuinely full.

Must not recommend retaining the local profiling revert as the final fix: it removed the cache-block message but caused GPU OOM on the same long-context workload, and the newer accounting includes real non-torch allocations.
Must ask the reporter to verify both successful startup and the original workload with eager execution before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical model-serving operator who builds CUDA-enabled Docker images, deploys quantized and tensor-parallel LLMs across multi-GPU systems, compares vLLM releases, and can test local source changes. Diagnostic memory logs from another technically advanced affected operator are folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, detailed, and persistent; supplies exact commands and traces, corrects maintainers when they focus on the secondary shared-GPU case, and reports both successful and failed experiments plainly.
